newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Arab National Bank rated A and A-1 -agency.
newsitem.headline: Arab National Bank rated A and A-1 -agency.

text.p: Riyadh-based Arab National Bank (ANB) long and short term ratings have been reaffirmed at A and A-1 by Capital Intelligence, the Cyprus-based specialist bank rating agency said in a statement.
Capital Intelligence has assigned a positive outlook to the bank and expects its credit ratings to improve over the coming 12-month period, the agency said in a press release on Thursday.
ANB had total assets of $8.5 billion at end 1995 and is 40 percent owned by Amman-based Arab Bank PLC. It is Saudi Arabia's fourth largest bank.
ANB's retail franchise has been developed aggressively in recent years following a complete re-engineering of operations and heavy investment in human resources.
The bank's performance has been kept relatively high considering that fundamental changes have been effected, reflecting ANB's good management and well focused strategies, Capital Intelligence said.
Key financial indicators remain very sound and the bank can benefit fully from its investment in technology and rationalisation within the next couple of years, it said.

Capital Intelligence added that profitability was likely to accelerate as depreciation fell in relative terms. The bank's 1996 net income is expected at around $120 million, up 10 percent on 1995, and should yield a return on average assets of about 1.4 percent.
